comentarios.texto: WHAT: In the non-credentialId branch, the loop deletes with the same `uid` and `externalCalendarId` of the current reference against every user calendar credential. WHY: With multiple calendar references, each reference now triggers deletes across all credentials, which produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

hist.text: The legacy branch (handleCancelBooking.ts:473-482) keeps the pre-existing behaviour of trying each reference's own uid/externalCalendarId against every calendar credential; the PR only runs it per reference (find->filter at :419), so each reference's event is deleted, with distinct uids, not duplicates. Failed wrong-provider deletes are swallowed by Promise.allSettled (:656), as before.

The PR changes reference selection to iterate every calendar reference (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:418–424), while the fallback sends each reference’s identifiers to every calendar credential without matching its provider or account (475–480). Wrong-account deletions can reject, as Office365 propagates deletion errors (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:111–121); these rejections also skip cancellation emails (handleCancelBooking.ts:656–665).

comentarios.texto: Legacy-store errors are now dropped without being logged. This is an observability problem: failures from the legacy store become invisible. Log these errors, as the previous code did.

hist.text: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes moved into goroutines that only call recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...) (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection); the previous log.Error calls for legacy failures were removed. Failures are still counted in metrics, so the effect is loss of error detail in logs, not a behaviour change.

The PR removes legacy-error logging; the replacement goroutines only pass error booleans to metrics in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55-56,112-113,139-140,165-166. Those helpers only observe histograms (pkg/apiserver/rest/metrics.go:54-61), so failure counts remain observable but the actual error details are lost, impairing diagnosis.
